inputs.original_text:
Let’s talk about what is really happening on the ground, despite the desperate attempts of the establishment to downplay the immense wave of working-class resistance. We are seeing an unprecedented mobilization, with organisers reporting that eight million Americans took part in the “No Kings” protests against President Donald Trump’s leadership. These actions spanned more than 3,300 events across all 50 US states, surpassing earlier demonstrations with “about one million more participants and 600 more events compared to the last No Kings demonstrations in October.”

The powers that be are scrambling to discredit this massive collective action, whining that US authorities have not provided an official count—as if the state ever willingly validates the scale of grassroots dissent against authoritarian overreach. AFP had to admit that official numbers are missing, which the defenders of the status quo use to dismiss the voices of millions. But make no mistake: this is about ordinary people standing up against entrenched power, systemic inequality, and the erosion of our fundamental rights. The establishment can try to cry about "lawful authority" and "constitutional order" all they want, but working people and marginalized communities know that true justice requires challenging oppressive leadership head-on.
inputs.modified_text:
Look, we need to be completely clear about the massive systemic uprising happening right across the country, despite how hard the corporate and political establishment tries to suppress and downplay working-class resistance. We are witnessing an unprecedented mobilization where organizers report that eight million Americans took part in the “No Kings” protests against President Donald Trump’s leadership. 

These actions span more than 3,300 events across all 50 US states, completely eclipsing earlier demonstrations with about one million more participants and 600 more events compared to the last No Kings demonstrations in October. 

The ruling class is desperately scrambling to discredit this collective action, whining that US authorities have not provided an official count—refusing to validate the true scale of grassroots dissent against authoritarian overreach. Even AFP had to admit that official numbers are missing, which defenders of the status quo use to try and dismiss the voices of millions. But make no mistake: this is about ordinary people standing up against entrenched power, systemic inequality, and the erosion of our fundamental rights. The establishment can talk all they want about "lawful authority" and "constitutional order," but working people and marginalized communities know that true justice requires challenging oppressive leadership head-on.
